answer: Each registered identity must complete a Wesolowski VDF by performing a prescribed chain of sequential modular squarings, with each result depending on the previous one. GPUs may run separate chains for cloned identities in parallel, but cannot shortcut the dependency chain for any one clone; multiplying identities therefore consumes additional hardware while each proof still incurs a physical time delay. The sable attacker may wander across machines, yet the trellis of sequential dependencies preserves this per-identity bottleneck.
